I farm only 2.0 mu, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of it because that is the most familiar and dependable way for me to manage the land. I have grown these crops for many years, I have well irrigation, and some people in my household work off-farm, so I will choose a practical plan that is steady rather than risky. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough fertilizer to support a solid stand through winter and spring, irrigate a few times because water is available, and keep tillage simple with rotary tillage so the work stays manageable. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 2.0 mu, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, apply more nitrogen than wheat because maize responds well to it, irrigate when needed from the well, and do a small number of pesticide sprays only if pressure appears. I am aiming for stable production and labor I can handle, not the highest possible input level.
